Expected: The shipped detector names neither the new document nor bus_monitor and still reads the speaker tap; a telemetry write failure returns false rather than raising; an unframeable block drops the streams instead of sending a guess.
The unit declares no User=, takes audio as a supplementary group, restricts address families to AF_UNIX, keeps ProtectSystem=strict, and runs only when the stored mode is bus.
Firstboot names the daemon, the unit and all three imports the daemon loads from beside itself; the health probe refuses without opening a device or writing a document.
Bus mode keeps the dsnoop at 0660 and gid 29 and no longer calls it the single reader; no other shipped configuration declares it.
The daemon is carried only behind the opt-in knob, is absent from the offline ISO payload, and the reimage checklist names re-install and re-authorisation as manual steps.
No auth-key literal or auth-key field exists in the repo, the payload, the materialised env or the secret schema; the setup script exposes no flag that would accept one.
Both forwarding keys are set in a dedicated late-sorting file under /etc/sysctl.d and no shared sysctl file is appended to.
Bring-up advertises the LAN CIDR, does not offer an exit node, and disables acceptance of the tunnel's DNS so Technitium's split-horizon is preserved.
An advertised route is reported as pending approval; the script never reports a route as active, which is a console-side fact it cannot observe.
LAN_CIDR admits the LAN and tunnel CIDRs and excludes the docker bridge range; a WAN or bridge caller is refused.
Every gated host uses remote_ip; no gated host uses client_ip, which would trust a forgeable X-Forwarded-For.
The service is absent from the default profile and publishes no host port; it is reachable only through Caddy on the docker bridge.
Only a digest reference under ghcr.io/tashfeenahmed/freellmapi passes; a floating tag fails, and so does a digest under a fork's namespace, a mirror or any other registry.
A valid key is accepted; an absent or wrong key is refused before any provider is contacted; a LAN caller is not exempt.
ai-cli remains bound to loopback or a docker bridge address and is never bound to the LAN; the assertion is made against the shipped setup rather than assumed.
No gateway route names an ai-cli endpoint and the two services share no credential, account or volume; the README states the wider-reach departure explicitly.
off requires neither probe answering; up requires either; the mapping is by condition and never by a truthiness check over a merged result.

A reachability timeout or refusal with nothing answering yields off and never up; readiness runs only on a reachable host; a listing that is absent-model, 500 or timeout leaves the state at up; only a success naming the target model yields ready.
waking holds within the deadline and becomes failed at and beyond it; no input sequence leaves the state waking indefinitely.
The magic packet targets the MAC from the deploy knob; the provider never resolves a MAC from the host address, which on this box returns the vEthernet adapter.
An alternate actuation provider satisfies the same seam and produces identical state transitions; selecting none is refused rather than silently succeeding.
A request arriving while not ready is held to the cap and answered; on expiry it is answered by the fallback provider, never returned as an error.
A single hold fires exactly one wake; a concurrent burst fires exactly one wake and all callers join the same flight rather than each starting one.
The timer sleeps the box only when idle has elapsed and no interactive session is attached; an attached session inhibits it regardless of idle time.
Each transition is reflected in the HTTP document, the broker topic and the monitor probe, and every document carries the instant the state was determined.
The rendezvous and relay mount the same named volume, declared once; a split-volume arrangement fails the check.
The volume appears in the local backup sources and is absent from the offsite set, because the key pair is not reproducible from the repo.
Both protocols are admitted from the LAN and tunnel CIDRs and rejected from the WAN, in both address families, asserted by address rather than by container name.
The isolation rules are installed in INPUT and ip6tables INPUT because these are host sockets; a DOCKER-USER rule fails the check, as does a v4-only ruleset.
No tracked config or document instructs a router forward for the remote-desktop ports; the README states service-mode installation and a distinct unattended password as requirements.

An expired wake deadline yields failed regardless of probe results; an unreachable host yields off even when a prior listing reported the model loaded; precedence is deadline, then reachability, then readiness.

A late joiner inherits the remaining deadline and cannot refresh it; every joiner observes one terminal outcome; a failed flight is cleared so a later request starts a new one rather than joining a dead flight.
The reference places no autogroup inside a groups entry and targets no tag in dst, because no device in this tailnet is tagged and a tag-only policy would accept nothing.

The setup script reads no local policy file, so it cannot report a local document as verification of a server-side policy; tailnet-lock state is still queried and reported as a warning rather than a failure.

No tracked script, unit, compose file or document invokes the upstream piped-shell installer; deployment is this repo's compose against the pinned digest, and the pin records digest, version and date.
A replay from a clean firewall installs the full rule set in both families; a replay over an existing set converges without duplicates; a stale CIDR's rule is removed rather than left behind.

After a reload or flush, a connection from a non-LAN, non-tunnel source to each documented TCP and UDP port is refused; the unit is ordered before and required by the services, so a rule-install failure stops the listeners instead of exposing them.

An arrival at each ordering boundary either joins the existing flight and sees its terminal outcome or starts exactly one new flight; no arrival observes a removed flight beside a stale not-ready state, and no arrival causes a duplicate wake.
Both containers declare restart: "no" so docker never starts them independently; the systemd unit Requires= and After= the isolation unit; a restart policy other than "no" fails the check.
Boot and a daemon restart do not start the containers; the owning unit starts them only after the isolation unit succeeds, and a fence failure prevents them starting.

A waiter continuation that reads state or requests another wake completes without deadlock; no wake, probe, broker publish or HTTP call is observed while the lock is held; waiters are notified from a snapshot taken under the lock and released before notification.

Only a fresh, well-formed, authenticated detached reading permits sleep; stale, absent, malformed and unauthenticated readings all inhibit sleep as though a session were attached; an explicit operator override is the sole path that sleeps despite an attached signal.

The hub publishes permit only when idle has elapsed and the session signal is a fresh detached reading; it never issues a sleep command. A consumer that is working declines a permitting verdict, and a stale session reading never yields permit.

Method: Run tests/test_wall_bluetooth_device.py alias and classification tests under pytest.
Expected: An alias is derived, recognisable, never address-shaped, and stable for a device that is still present: a newcomer never renames a device already on the glass, a rename frees an alias that is nonetheless not handed to another device while the first is present, and a departed device releases its alias. A phone classifies as an input and a headset as an output, including through the two opposite handsfree roles.

Method: Run tests/test_wall_bluetooth_device.py spool and drain tests under pytest.
Expected: Every request in a burst survives to the applier and is performed once, in sequence order; a replayed sequence is refused; a request the applier cannot understand is consumed rather than re-read forever; a request from a previous epoch is ignored; the bound leaves the remainder spooled for the observe verb rather than discarding it; a contended lock leaves the work to the holder and is not a failure, while a lock that cannot be opened fails loudly and leaves the spool untouched.

Method: Run tests/test_wall_bluetooth_device.py backend and document tests under pytest.
Expected: An untrustworthy document reads as "do not know" with an empty inventory and an unavailable status, never as an empty room; the switch backend's own blocks pass through verbatim; a route naming a device that is gone is dropped; a device whose BlueZ name is its own address publishes no address and costs no other device its row; a publish that cannot finish inside its budget reports "do not know"; `request_landed` asks the applier that minted the sequence; a missing applier refuses the verb rather than spooling a request.

The two new verbs are shaped exactly and refuse a defaulted direction or a named window length; a pairing block the broker did not send is omitted rather than invented, while a malformed one fails the whole status; the passkey crosses verbatim with its leading zero; the discoverable control is hidden entirely when the broker cannot answer; the button label is the state and the tap asks for the other one; an untrusted device offers both pair and trust; revoking trust asks first; a locked pane shows no pairing state at all.

A saved archive restores the sign-in onto an emptied profile; a save refuses with no sign-in to save and with a keyring present; a restore refuses a held profile, refuses to replace an existing sign-in without the flag, refuses an archive carrying no cookie store, and refuses whole -- leaving the partition untouched -- on any unsafe member; a stale lock from a dead process does not block a restore.

The derived identity drops both runtime-only tokens and is an ordinary browser string; an application release and a runtime patch do not move it; an engine major does, exactly as a browser update would; nothing is invented from a string that is not understood, and a session that cannot be read or refuses the call leaves the default in place rather than taking the player down.

Method: Run tests/test_litellm_pin_route.py precedence tests, which DRIVE the shipped script against a preseeded chain.
Expected: Both precedence guards are exercised in the state where they must FIRE, not only in the silent state where nothing precedes the fence. An ACCEPT placed at or above the ts-input jump - the shape the remote-desktop fence installs - makes the script exit non-zero naming the offending rule, and an ACCEPT above the DOCKER-USER jump in FORWARD does the same. This is the branch that had never once executed: round 6 shipped an unguarded grep -v whose no-match exit killed the script on the CORRECT path, so only a test that reaches the firing branch can tell a working guard from a fatal one. Mutation-checked: neutering either guard turns the matching test red.

Method: Run tests/test_litellm_pin_route.py reapply-window tests, including a stub-injected insert failure mid-rebuild.
Expected: A rebuild deletes the old rules before inserting the new ones, so the state BETWEEN them is the property under test rather than the exit code. A blanket deny for the pinned source is installed first and removed only after every read-back has passed, so every intermediate state is more restrictive than both the old and the new rule set. A successful run leaves no guard behind and the three real rules in the required order; a refusal that happens after the rebuild leaves no allow below the last deny; and an insert that FAILS at deny-all - the only injection point that would otherwise leave the chain empty for this source - leaves the blanket deny in place above every allow. Mutation-checked: removing the guard inserts turns the mid-rebuild case red while the other two stay green, which is what makes the guard load-bearing rather than decorative.

Method: Run tests/test_litellm_pin_route.py hold-decision table under pytest, including non-mapping readiness documents.
Expected: decide_hold is total over its declared argument. The readiness answer is whatever json.loads produced, so a body of [], "ready" or 5 is valid JSON that is not a document; the narrower None check let those reach .get and raise AttributeError straight out of the pre-call hook. That mattered beyond the crash: the gateway in front classifies our refusals as retryable by substring-matching 503 and unavailable, and an AttributeError carries neither, so a malformed readiness answer would have presented as the gateway being down for BOTH lanes rather than as a sleeping dev PC. Any non-mapping is now read as no-oracle, which is the same fact the None case already encoded.

Method: Run tests/test_litellm_pin_route.py long-chain test, which drives the shipped script against a chain padded past the pipe buffer.
Expected: No parser closes its pipe before its producer has finished. An early-exiting `awk '{print; exit}'` or a `head -1` makes iptables take SIGPIPE and die 141; `pipefail` adopts that status and `set -e` ends the script, so the fence dies with no message on a chain that is entirely healthy - the same silent-failure signature as the round 6 blocker. The trigger is not a long chain but a match EARLY with a large tail after it, which is this box's measured shape: ts-input is INPUT position 1 and every other rule sits below it. Reproduced outside the harness, the pipeline survives 20 trailing rules and dies at 2000, which is simply where the listing passes the 64 KiB pipe buffer; the other fixtures in this file use a handful of rules and cannot expose it. Every parser now consumes its whole input and keeps the first match. `|| true` is explicitly NOT the fix, because it would also swallow a genuine failure to read the chain. Mutation-checked: restoring the early-exit form on a single parser turns this case red while the short-chain cases stay green.

Method: Run tests/test_litellm_pin_route.py replay test, which drives the shipped script twice against one chain.
Expected: The unit re-runs on every boot and after any firewall reload or compose recreate, so convergence is the normal case rather than an edge one. Two runs leave byte-identical chains, exactly three marker rules per chain, and no reapply guard behind either. This is re-proved rather than assumed because the guard is a fourth marker rule added and removed inside a single run: an exclusion that was slightly wrong would either leave one behind on each run or delete a real rule alongside it, and neither shows up in a single run. Mutation-checked: dropping the guard exclusion from the rebuild loops is caught.

Method: Run tests/test_litellm_pin_route.py exemption test, which executes scripts/validate_config.py against a throwaway stack tree.
Expected: The build gate's one named exemption covers one DIRECTIVE, not one unit. homehub-litellm.service is allowed PartOf=docker.service because no Wants=+After= form keeps a RemainAfterExit oneshot alive across a docker restart, so the usual remedy does not apply; but Requires=docker.service on the same unit is the 2026-08-09 defect that SIGTERM'd firstboot mid-LV-move and must still fail the build. The first version of the exemption filtered the MERGED dependency set, so the Requires regression would have been waved through by an exemption written for PartOf while the comment beside it promised the opposite. Provenance is now kept per directive. The check is EXECUTED against a copied tree rather than grepped, and the copy is the six files the check actually reads rather than all of stack/. Mutation-checked: restoring the merged filter turns this case red.

Method: Run tests/test_deploy_stack.py protection tests under pytest.

The box's .env is the only copy of its configuration and credentials and is not in the repo, so a tool that treated it and .env.example as the same file would take the hub down and destroy credentials that exist nowhere else, while reporting a successful delivery. .env.example IS delivered, because refusing it 'to be safe' would mean every new knob arrived undocumented on the one machine that has to be configured. Mutation-checked: emptying the protected set turns this red.

Method: Run tests/test_deploy_stack.py boundary and plan tests under pytest.
Expected: The hub/panel boundary is decided by what the HUB uses - its compose file and its firstboot - and not by the directory name, because the names mislead in both directions: panel-audio/ is installed by the PANEL's firstboot and is inert on the hub, while wall-shell/ is bind-mounted by caddy and served FROM the hub. Excluding by name would have dropped a hub-side directory and kept a panel-side one. The plan separates absent from stale from identical, and a file present on the box but untracked in the repo appears in NONE of them - it is left alone, never deleted, which is what protects docker-compose.override.yml, llm-gateway.env and the deployed panel-access/app bundle. Mutation-checked: dropping panel-audio from the exclusion turns this red.

Method: Run tests/test_deploy_stack.py placement and provenance tests under pytest.
Expected: Placement truncates in place and keeps the inode; install, mv, cp and tar -x all unlink and recreate, which detaches a compose bind mount so the container serves the old bytes through a reload that reports success. tar is used only to unpack into a staging directory, never over the live tree. The payload comes from `git archive <revision>` rather than the working tree, so an uncommitted edit cannot reach a box, and a dirty tree is reported out loud rather than silently ignored - this repo has already paid for working-tree-as-truth once. Hashes are of the bytes git would deliver, LF rather than the CRLF a Windows checkout holds, so a Windows clone does not mark every text file stale for ever. A --report path that already exists is refused, reusing the panel release lane's rule that evidence is never overwritten.

Method: Run tests/test_devpc_wake.py residency tests under pytest.
Expected: A LISTED MODEL IS NOT A READY ONE. The state stays `up` with a reason naming residency as unverified, and only a completion promotes it to `ready`. This is the defect restated: the assertion in TC-988 previously read `== "ready"` on a listing alone, so the test encoded the bug. Both Ollama and llama-server list a model that is configured and not resident, so the first request after a wake still paid a full load. Mutation-checked: promoting on the listing turns this red.

Method: Run tests/test_devpc_wake.py poller and expiry tests under pytest.
Expected: THE POLLER FIRES NO COMPLETIONS AT ALL - twenty-five cheap passes produce zero. On a fifteen-second beat a single completion per poll is a permanent VRAM lease: the weights could never be evicted and OLLAMA_KEEP_ALIVE, whose job is to hand the card back when the Owner wants to play a game, would be defeated by the service watching it. Separately, a verified residency EXPIRES after the TTL, so a model the keep-alive has since evicted stops being advertised as ready. Mutation-checked: making the cheap path deep turns this red.

Method: Run tests/test_devpc_wake.py non-blocking and single-flight tests under pytest.
Expected: A DEEP ASK RETURNS IMMEDIATELY and the probe runs behind it. A synchronous probe would block /state for the length of a cold model load, and the hold hook polls /state with a short timeout while holding a request - it reads a timeout as no-oracle and REFUSES, so a sleeping box would become a hard failure instead of a wait. The probe is handed to a background thread, nothing runs on the caller's thread, and twenty concurrent asks produce ONE in-flight probe rather than twenty model loads.
